proof_attempt_summary: Field-tier sharp partial-ID of the always-takers ADRF (Lee-Liu 2025 deferred covariate case): sharp support-function/Dinkelbach identified set + iff pointwise-plugin sharpness condition C + plug-in consistency estimator, all proven; novelty PASS. tldr: The unresolved sufficient-set case in Lee and Liu's continuous-treatment Lee bounds is a law-level aggregation problem, not a pointwise trimming problem. For a fixed dose d, the always-takers average dose-response function is interval identified because the sufficient-set restriction implies an observable Frechet band [underline_pi_d(X), overline_pi_d(X)] for the conditional always-taker mass, while the endpoint averages are ratios with the common denominator E[pi(X)]. The proposal characterizes each sharp endpoint as the value of a global support-function problem over measurable selector functions pi in Pi_d(P), reduces that linear-fractional program to a scalar Dinkelbach root, and isolates a root-normalized common-threshold condition under which the naive pointwise Frechet plug-in is exactly sharp. A kernel-localized doubly robust endpoint handle then targets the smooth-root submodel where the finite-bandwidth transformed score equals the population transform up to an explicit O(h_n^2) bias under local dose smoothness, the root derivative is fixed at -E[pi_sigma^*(X)], and honest coverage at tie and boundary laws remains the explicit open question.
gap: LeeLiu2025ContinuousLee identifies the continuous-treatment always-takers ADRF under sufficient values, but in the sufficient-set covariate case the conditional always-taker share is only constrained by an observable Frechet band and the paper leaves the covariate-aggregated sharp identified set unresolved.
fill: The project fills that gap with a measurable-selector support-function characterization, a scalar Dinkelbach threshold representation, a primitive collapse criterion for exact pointwise plug-in sharpness, and a regular-regime endpoint estimator whose expansion keeps the finite-bandwidth kernel bias explicit and uses the h_n-scaled variance normalization implied by local dose localization.
